video.title: Why harness is SO expensive..
video.genre: AI explainer and opinion, partly screen-shared

protocol.note: Drafted from the transcript alone, without seeing any jevcut output or other labels.
protocol.times_from: Lemonfox transcript; seconds in the source, so labels survive re-transcription

clips.why: Hook: 'the cost of the model is very different than the cost of the harness that surrounds it' (drops 'But'). Chat is a thin harness; early adopters use thick ones (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) where you work through the harness; payoff: per Anthropic, agents and multi-agent systems cost 4-15x more.

Hook: a tiny 25-token prompt (create a file with the alphabet) costs about a cent at Opus 5 pricing -- the same prompt in Claude Code costs 37 cents, 'nearly 30 times more expensive right off the bat.' Payoff: harnesses add 8,000-30,000 tokens to every message, 'like a toll gate you have to pay to get to the model' (163.2); 166.1 adds that the overhead is the system prompt. Demo is on screen but every number is spoken.

Hook: prompt caching could be lucrative from Anthropic's side. Back-of-envelope: an H100 rents for ~$3/hour, one 1M-token context fits on one card, 12 five-minute slots -> about $70/hour of caching revenue per H100, 'which is huge' (404.3). Later end adds the honest caveat (quantizing 1M context into 80GB).

also_ok.why: Your prompt isn't sent once: the harness and model loop (check file exists, create it, write contents) until the model decides it's done -- 'a lot of back and forth for even a simple task.' Clear explanation, but its cost payoff (each round trip pays the toll gate) comes later and leans on earlier material.

Vendors keep users in their walled garden by selling a subscription on the model layer and letting harnesses run under it, so you're not 'having an anxiety attack' over agent spend. A fine short take, but it is the run-up into the sponsor segment.

negatives.why: Open vs closed model race with 'as you can see' leaderboard narration; setup, not the video's point.
Harness-by-harness prices (37c, 11c, 7c, 2.5c): numbers are tempting but it opens 'the same prompt from earlier' and is a readout.
Anthropic pricing page read off screen (cache pricing tiers, one-hour caching).
One-hour cache speculation (spill to SSD, $10/M writes): depends on the H100 math just before and is guesswork.
Sponsor read (Kline Pass), including the 'what if you wanted a flexible subscription' setup.
